items.text: This roadmap is also about building a genuine high-value skill portfolio, not just passing one interview.
It can compound into leadership, advisory, consulting, or building a product.

blocks.heading: Indian Product Hiring Has Shifted Toward Work

items.text: You do not need to write production code, but you need enough working knowledge of APIs, databases, and system constraints to have a real conversation with engineers about what is hard, what is fast, and what will quietly break something else.

Build this by reading your own product's API docs, learning basic SQL to pull your own numbers instead of asking an analyst, and sitting in on a few engineering standups even before anyone asks you to.
Almost every "how to become a PM" story in India collapses into one of three real entry doors.
The most common path into product management in India.
You have 1+ years in a company with a real product function, or you are early-career and want a structured, mentored entry.
Sequence matters more than most self-taught roadmaps admit.
Before touching any product tool, understand how the specific industry or company type you want to join actually makes money.

blocks.sourceSectionTitle: APM programs and who else hires juniors

rows: Structured APM programs
Flipkart, Google, and a small set of large product companies run defined, mentored APM tracks with rotations.
Often campus-hiring only or a narrow annual application window; high competition for a small number of seats.
Product companies that also hire APMs off-cycle
Amazon, Razorpay, Swiggy, Zoho, Freshworks, PhonePe, and many funded startups hire junior PMs outside a formal APM brand name.
Less structured mentorship than a named program, but a real door if you missed the campus window.
Business-analyst or associate-consultant to PM
Consulting and analytics-heavy firms sometimes move strong analysts into product-adjacent or full PM roles internally.
Slower and less visible than a direct APM hire, but a legitimate side door if you are already inside a large organisation.
Product School PM certification / similar batch courses
Worth it, conditionally
Useful for structure, peer accountability, and a portfolio project if you are starting from zero, but the certificate itself rarely moves an interview; the case study you build during it does.
CSPO (Certified Scrum Product Owner)
Skip unless required
Tests Scrum ceremonies, not product judgment. Useful only if a specific employer explicitly lists it, or you need Agile vocabulary fast for a services-to-product move.
PMI-ACP or general project-management certifications
Skip
These certify project delivery, not product decision-making. They rarely appear on Indian PM job descriptions and will not substitute for a real case study in an interview.
Reforge, Pragmatic Institute, or similar practitioner programs
Worth it if you can afford it
Built by working PMs, taught with real frameworks and case studies rather than generic theory. Priced high; treat it as a skill accelerator, not a credential to list.
Free courses (Coursera, Google, university MOOCs)
Fine as a starting point
Good for vocabulary and frameworks at zero cost. Do not stop here, a free certificate with no applied project behind it reads as intention, not readiness.

visuals.heading: Proof of Work Before the Title

items.text: Own one thing end-to-end wherever you already are: a feature, a process gap, or a small internal tool nobody has claimed.
Write it up the way a PM would, the problem, the options you considered, the trade-off you picked, and the measured result, not the way an engineer, designer, or analyst would.
Build or improve one small thing outside work if your current role gives you no real ownership.
Get one honest outside opinion from someone already working in product before you spend months applying on the strength of a case study nobody else has stress-tested.
